patch_description: Instead of naive pairwise proportional radius shrinking, this approach: (1) initializes 26 centers on a staggered hexagonal lattice (rows 5,5,5,5,4,3) since hexagonal is near-optimal locally, (2) computes optimal radii for the given centers exactly via linear programming (maximize sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance), and (3) iteratively refines centers using a deterministic "pressure" force (each circle is pushed away from its tightest contacts and walls), re-solving the LP after each refinement sweep. This alternating optimization (centers via geometric forces, radii via LP) is fundamentally different from the original one-shot proportional scaling and yields a much larger, provably valid sum of radii.
